questions.question: Which statement best separates FlashAttention from approximate attention?
options: It evaluates the same dense attention formula in an IO-aware tiled order
It randomly deletes most attention scores
It replaces softmax with a linear activation
It guarantees bitwise-identical output on every backend
questions.explanation: FlashAttention is exact at the mathematical-operation level. Tiling and online softmax change execution and floating-point order, not the dense attention rule.

questions.question: A materialized implementation stores score and probability tensors for B=2, H=16, and sequence length N. What happens to those bytes when N doubles and the other terms stay fixed?
options: They stay constant
They double
They grow by about four times
They grow by about eight times
questions.explanation: Both tensors contain B x H x N x N elements, so doubling N multiplies the quadratic term by four.

questions.question: Which memory term can still dominate long-context autoregressive serving after tiled attention removes the full score matrix?
options: The scalar learning rate
The KV cache across layers and concurrent sequences
The model filename
The number of benchmark warmup iterations
questions.explanation: The KV cache grows with batch or concurrency, KV heads, sequence length, head dimension, dtype bytes, and layer count.

questions.question: What should production code do when a forced fused SDPA backend does not support an input shape?
options: Silently claim the fused kernel ran
Drop tokens until the call succeeds
Apply an explicit fail-closed or exact-fallback policy and record the dispatch reason
Disable all correctness checks
questions.explanation: Unsupported dispatch is an operational state. The service should reject intentionally or use an enabled exact fallback, with telemetry showing what happened.

questions.question: Why should correctness tests compare both outputs and Q/K/V gradients?
options: Training can have a correct-looking forward result while the backward path is unsupported or numerically wrong
Gradients determine GPU memory capacity
Outputs are never useful
Gradient checks guarantee a universal speedup
questions.explanation: A training release depends on both passes. Backend, dtype, dropout, masking, and shape can affect backward support and numerical behavior.

questions.question: Which benchmark comparison is valid?
options: One unsynchronized launch of each backend with different shapes
The fastest observed run after deleting OOM results
Repeated synchronized measurements with matched shapes, warmup, dtype, mask, runtime, and device
A kernel microbenchmark used as proof of end-to-end service speed
questions.explanation: Matched inputs, warmup, synchronization, repetitions, and environment make the kernel comparison interpretable; end-to-end performance still needs a separate benchmark.

questions.question: Which event should trigger the FlashAttention release matrix to run again?
options: Only a change to the lesson title
A new head layout, sequence policy, runtime version, or hardware family
Only a lower cloud bill
Never, once one A100 benchmark passes
questions.explanation: Kernel eligibility and performance depend on shapes and the software/hardware stack, so those changes invalidate prior dispatch and benchmark evidence.
